name: Oatmeal / fibre for gut-skin axis

lead: The idea is that fibre-rich foods such as oatmeal feed gut bacteria, which produce short-chain fatty acids and support a healthier gut, with downstream benefits for skin. It is a common gut-skin axis talking point in appearance communities.

Wikipedia describes dietary fibre research as preliminary overall, with associations such as lower cardiovascular risk and relief of constipation, and notes oat beta-glucan lowers LDL cholesterol. The page does not discuss skin outcomes.

paras: Fermentable fibres are broken down by large-intestine bacteria into short-chain fatty acids (butyrate, propionate, acetate), which are linked to gut-barrier and immune functions.
Wikipedia notes inulin can cause flatulence and digestive distress above about 15 g per day, and isolated fermentable fibres may cause bloating and gas.

lead: Dietary fibre is the portion of plant food not fully broken down by human digestive enzymes, including cellulose, resistant starch and pectins [1]. Oats and barley contain beta-glucan, a soluble viscous fermentable fibre that has been shown to lower LDL cholesterol with regular intake [1].

In the gut-skin axis idea discussed in appearance communities, fibre is thought to help skin by feeding gut bacteria that make short-chain fatty acids [1]. Wikipedia notes that these acids are linked to gut-barrier and immune functions, but describes fibre research as preliminary and does not discuss skin health [1].
No studies of oatmeal or fibre for skin appearance were found in the sources reviewed.
infobox: Gut bacteria fermentation to short-chain fatty acids

paras: Fermentable fibres feed bacteria in the large intestine, which produce short-chain fatty acids and gases; the main acids are butyrate, propionate and acetate. Wikipedia links them to steadier blood glucose, lower LDL, nourishment of colon cells and immune and gut-barrier functions [1].

No studies found on oatmeal or fibre for skin or acne outcomes. For general health, Wikipedia reports associations between high fibre intake and lower cardiovascular and type 2 diabetes risk and relief of constipation, described as preliminary [1].

Inulin can cause flatulence and digestive distress in most people above about 15 g per day, isolated fermentable fibres may cause bloating, and finely ground insoluble fibre may cause constipation [1].

lore.intro: Fibre and oats are discussed in gut-focused skin routines.

claims.claim: Oatmeal and fibre improve skin by improving gut health
